newsitem.title: UK: European bourses rise above U.S. rate rise.
newsitem.headline: European bourses rise above U.S. rate rise.

text.p: European stock markets held on to most of their gains on Wednesday but lost a little of their shine as economists fretted at the possibility of a further tightening of American monetary policy.
Speculation that the Federal Reserve could come back with another rate rise in May to head off inflationary pressures and record U.S. durable goods orders for February lent the dollar support.
The dollar-boosting durable goods figures followed Tuesday's decision of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making open market committee to increase rates by a quarter of a percentage point.
U.S. Treasury bonds fell in the wake of the data, which also weighed down early share trading on Wall Street.
By the time European markets closed the Dow Jones index was still a few points adrift but moved back into the black shortly after.
Traders zeroed in on Fed comments accompanying Tuesday's rate rise that hinted at a further monetary tightening at the May meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
"It has made the market reassess the future of monetary policy. I think another rate rise pretty soon is now being contemplated," said one trader in London.
Despite that, European equity markets reacted with relief that Tuesday's pre-emptive strike against inflation was out of the way.
The region's biggest bourses -- London, Paris and Frankfurt -- retreated from sharp gains in the morning but still ended the day with good progress.
German shares made the most progress, the 30-share DAX index jumping more than two percent by the close of floor trade as bank shares came back into vogue.
Daimler-Benz also hit an all-time high of 133.5 marks after reporting better-than-expected 1996 results and the IBIS DAX index closed screen-based trade up 1.9 percent at 3,439.22 points.

In London, the blue chip FTSE 100 index reclaimed the 4,300 point level after snapping a six-day losing streak on Tuesday. The benchmark index added 30.8 points to 4,301.5 but closed well off its highs.
Dealers and analysts said they expected investors to focus more on domestic factors now the Fed tightening was out of the way.
"We still have our own situation to take on board, the end of the first quarter, a long weekend and the likelihood of a rate rise soon after the (May 1) election," one dealer said.
Among individual stocks, impressive results and an upbeat trading statement from Next Plc drove the UK retailer's shares 21-1/2p higher to 617-1/2p.
French stocks finished higher but a few points off its best of the day after the early drop on Wall Street and U.S. data.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 24.48 points, or 0.93 percent, at 2,648.73, while the CAC-40 March futures contract rose 17 points to 2,644. Volume was 7.97 billion francs.
Electrical equipment supplier Schneider rose 6.26 percent to 320.70 francs on better than expected results.
On the foreign exchange market, the dollar gathered momentum in late European business and ended above 1.69 marks and 124 yen after the durable goods data.

"We have shifted away from Fed watching back to economy watching and this is the first reading we have had on the economy since the rate move yesterday," David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.
The dollar jumped to session peaks of 1.6955 marks after the figures, but settled off highs at 1.6910 marks and 124.20 yen.
Against the yen, analysts said the dollar was likely to push towards the 125 yen level on expectations that Japanese interest rates will stay low.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6910 marks and 124.20 yen compared with 1.6919 marks and 123.92 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS -- CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 30.8, or 0.72 percent, at 4,301.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index closed up 24.48 points, or 0.93 percent, at 2,648.73.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 68.98 points, or 2.06 percent, at 3,418.12. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended up 64.29, or 1.9 percent, at 3,418.12.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended in London at $348.75 against $349.15 on Tuesday. Silver closed two cents firmer at $5.15.
